mainTopic: Redemption by relatives, the laws of the נרצע, and whether a כהן may be given a שפחה כנענית or take a יפת תאר
overview: The גמרא first finishes a discussion about which redemptions relatives may make. It explains that the triple 'יגאלנו' teaches that the closest relative redeems first. It then returns to the משנה: a נרצע is acquired by piercing his ear, and he goes free at the יובל or when his master dies. רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue about which tools may be used for the piercing, and the גמרא traces their argument to two different ways of reading the פסוק. A ברייתא teaches that a כהן who is an עבד עברי is not pierced, because he would become a בעל מום and could not return to his full family status. רב נחמן uses that ברייתא to prove that a master may give a כהן slave a שפחה כנענית. Finally, רב and שמואל argue, in two versions, about whether a כהן may take a יפת תאר. A ברייתא then starts explaining that law word by word, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: That verse makes redemption an obligation
steps.stepSummary: The verse about redeeming a slave sold to a non-Jew is needed to make redeeming him a חובה, even according to רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed to make redemption an obligation, even according to רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question by saying the verse about the slave's redemption has its own job: it makes redeeming him a requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the verse is used to create an obligation, it cannot also serve as the source for which cases can be redeemed by relatives. The obligation holds even for רבי יהושע, who normally does not require redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: to make it a fixed obligation
a תנא who holds redemption is generally optional

phrases.english: That one is to establish it as an obligation,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the verse the גמרא was just asking about, about redeeming a slave sold to a non-Jew.

phrases.english: and even according to רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section, across the page break.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the verse to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse was thought to be extra and therefore available to teach something about relatives redeeming.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is needed to make redemption obligatory, so it is not extra.

steps.title: Proof from the triple 'he shall redeem him'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the three times 'יגאלנו' include all redemptions in a set order; the גמרא suggests this includes a בית בערי חומה and an עבד עברי sold to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Why does the verse say 'he shall redeem him' three times? To include all redemptions, that they are redeemed in this order. Doesn't this mean houses in walled cities and a Hebrew slave sold to a Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and tries to use it to prove that relatives can redeem a house in a walled city and a Hebrew slave sold to a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse repeats 'יגאלנו' three times, and the ברייתא says the extra words add other kinds of redemption. The גמרא suggests the added cases are exactly the two cases in doubt, which would settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear; introduces a proof

phrases.english: Come and hear:
What does the verse come to teach
'He shall redeem him,' 'he shall redeem him,' 'he shall redeem him': three times?
To include all redemptions
that they are redeemed in this order.
Is it not referring to houses of walled cities
and a Hebrew slave sold to a Jew?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier attempt is answered, a new proof is tried.
steps.raayaObject: That relatives can redeem a house in a walled city and a Hebrew slave sold to a Jew.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the triple 'יגאלנו' as including all redemptions.

steps.title: No, it includes open-area houses and ancestral fields
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא includes בתי חצרים and שדה אחוזה, not the two cases in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means houses in open areas and an ancestral field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by reading the ברייתא as talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is about בתי חצרים and שדה אחוזה, it says nothing about a walled-city house or a slave sold to a Jew. So the question stays open.

phrases.english: No, houses in open areas and an ancestral field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the ברייתא refers to walled-city houses and slaves sold to Jews.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as including other cases.

steps.title: Open-area houses already have an explicit verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the verse already says בתי חצרים are treated like fields, so why would the triple 'יגאלנו' be needed for them?
steps.simpleTranslation: About houses in open areas it is written explicitly: 'They shall be reckoned like the field of the land'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection by pointing out that the Torah already teaches the law of בתי חצרים openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a verse already compares open-area houses to fields, there seems to be no need for the extra 'יגאלנו' to include them. That would push the ברייתא back toward the original proof.

phrases.english: Concerning houses in open areas, it is written explicitly about them:
'They shall be reckoned like the field of the land'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא includes בתי חצרים and שדה אחוזה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit verse already covers them, so the extra words would be unnecessary.

steps.title: A closer relative comes first
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the ברייתא is teaching the order: the closer relative redeems first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the closer relative comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains what the ברייתא adds even for open-area houses and fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explicit verse teaches that these houses can be redeemed, but not who goes first. The words 'in this order' in the ברייתא teach that the closest relative has priority, so the rejection in step 3 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The triple 'יגאלנו' teaches the order of redemption (closest relative first) for בתי חצרים and שדה אחוזה. It does not prove anything about a walled-city house or a slave sold to a Jew.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
To teach that the closer relative comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new detail the extra words teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words seemed unnecessary for open-area houses.
steps.terutzMaskana: They teach the order of relatives, so they are needed.

steps.title: A pierced slave is acquired by piercing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: a נרצע is acquired through רציעה, based on the verse about piercing his ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the pierced slave is acquired through piercing, as it is written: 'And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and gives the verse for the rule that a נרצע is acquired by piercing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that an עבד עברי who chooses to stay after six years is acquired anew by having his ear pierced. The source is the verse where the master pierces his ear with an awl.

keyTerms.meaning: a slave whose ear was pierced

phrases.english: And the pierced slave is acquired through piercing.
As it is written:
'And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, etc.'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נרצע is acquired through piercing his ear, learned from שמות 21:6.

steps.title: He goes free when the master dies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a נרצע goes free at יובל or at the master's death; the word 'ועבדו' shows he serves only the master, not the son or daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he acquires himself through the Jubilee and through the master's death, as it is written: 'And he shall serve him' — but not the son and not the daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and gives the source for the master's death setting him free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ועבדו' means 'he shall serve him', the master himself. So once the master dies, the slave does not pass to the master's son or daughter, and he goes free.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with a regular עבד עברי (one not pierced), whose rules about serving the master's son are different. Here we are talking only about a נרצע.

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹנֶה אֶת עַצְמוֹ בַּיּוֹבֵל וּבְמִיתַת הָאָדוֹן.
phrases.english: And he acquires himself through the Jubilee and through the master's death.
As it is written: 'And he shall serve him'
phrases.notes: Same verse, שמות 21:6.

phrases.aramaic: – וְלֹא אֶת הַבֵּן וְלֹא אֶת הַבַּת.
phrases.english: — but not the son and not the daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקוֹנֶה אֶת עַצְמוֹ בַּיּוֹבֵל וּבְמִיתַת הָאָדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next line of the משנה about the נרצע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נרצע serves only the master himself; he goes free at the master's death.

steps.title: 'Forever' means until the Jubilee
steps.stepSummary: The word 'לעולם' does not mean for all time; it means until the יובל, which is why a נרצע goes free at יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Forever' means the 'forever' of the Jubilee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the other half of the משנה: that a נרצע goes free at יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says he serves 'לעולם', which sounds like forever. The גמרא reads it as the full span up to יובל, so the יובל ends his service.

keyTerms.meaning: the Jubilee year, every fiftieth year

steps.whatToRemember: A נרצע is acquired by piercing, and goes free either when the master dies ('ועבדו', not his children) or at יובל ('לעולם' means until יובל).

phrases.english: 'Forever' — the 'forever' of the Jubilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the sources for the משנה line quoted in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לעולם' in the verse means until the יובל, so a נרצע goes free at יובל.

steps.title: Any handheld tool may be used for piercing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that the word 'ולקחת' includes any tool held in the hand, not only an awl.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The verse says 'an awl.' That alone would only teach an awl. How do we know that a thorn, a needle, a drill, or a stylus may also be used? The verse says 'And you shall take,' which includes anything taken in the hand. This is the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about which tools may be used to pierce the ear of an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names a מרצע, an awl, so we might think only an awl works. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads the extra word 'ולקחת' as widening the rule to any tool you can hold in your hand, even a thorn.

keyTerms.meaning: An awl, a pointed tool for making holes
The verse teaches; introduces the source for a rule
To include; to add more cases to the rule
And you shall take; the word used here to include more tools

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"An awl": from this I would only know an awl;
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק about piercing the ear, דברים 15:17.

phrases.english: from where do we include a sharp thorn and a thorn
and a needle, a drill, and a stylus?
The verse says: "And you shall take"
to include anything that is taken in the hand.
These are the words of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״מַרְצֵעַ״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מַרְצֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of רציעה from step 6, now asking which tool may be used
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, any handheld tool may be used for רציעה.

steps.title: Only metal tools may be used, and a large awl is included
steps.stepSummary: רבי argues that only metal tools may be used, like the awl itself. A second teaching says 'המרצע' includes a large awl.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Just as an awl is special because it is made of metal, so too any metal tool may be used. Another explanation: 'the awl' comes to include the large awl.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and limits the tools to metal ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the awl in the פסוק is a model. Other tools count only if they share its key feature, being metal, so a thorn would not work. The 'other explanation' learns from the extra letter ה in 'המרצע' that even an especially large awl may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Special; the key feature that marks something

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי here with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, and he allows fewer tools.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone always means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Just as an awl is special in that it is made of metal,
so too anything made of metal may be used.
Another explanation: "the awl"
comes to include the large awl.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: מָה מַרְצֵעַ מְיוּחָד שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, only metal tools may be used for רציעה; 'המרצע' also includes a large awl.

steps.title: The piercing is done on the earlobe
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reports that יודן בריבי taught that the piercing is done only on the earlobe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: יודן בריבי used to teach that when they pierce, they pierce only the earlobe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question: where on the ear the piercing is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יודן בריבי holds that the hole is made in the soft lower part of the ear, the earlobe. This sets up the חכמים's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The earlobe, the soft lower part of the ear

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Yudan the distinguished one used to teach:
phrases.notes: 'בריבי' is a title of honor, roughly 'the distinguished one.'

phrases.english: When they pierce,
they pierce only the earlobe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: יוּדָן בְּרִיבִּי הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side question about where the רציעה is done
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to יודן בריבי, the רציעה is done on the earlobe.

steps.title: The Sages prove the piercing is on the upper ear
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that a כהן עבד עברי is not pierced because it makes him blemished. An earlobe hole would not be a blemish, so the piercing must be on the upper ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages say: A Hebrew slave who is a כהן is not pierced, because it would make him a בעל מום. If you say they pierce the earlobe, how would that make him a בעל מום? So the piercing must be only on the upper part of the ear.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack יודן בריבי's view by pointing to a known rule about a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a כהן who is an עבד עברי is not pierced, because the hole would make him a בעל מום, unfit to serve in the מקדש. A small hole in the soft earlobe does not count as a blemish, so the rule only makes sense if the piercing is in the upper ear, which is a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone with a physical blemish; a כהן with one cannot serve in the מקדש
The upper part of the ear

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a known הלכה about a כהן can settle a factual question, here the exact place on the ear for רציעה.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
A Hebrew slave who is a priest is not pierced,
because he would become blemished.
And if you say they pierce the earlobe,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ עֶבֶד עִבְרִי כֹּהֵן יֵעָשֶׂה בַּעַל מוּם?
phrases.english: how would a Hebrew slave who is a priest become blemished?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין נִרְצָע אֶלָּא בְּגוֹבַהּ שֶׁל אֹזֶן.
phrases.english: So he is pierced only on the upper part of the ear.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי כֹּהֵן נִרְצָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against יודן בריבי's earlobe view
steps.kashyaTarget: יודן בריבי's claim that the piercing is on the earlobe
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן is not pierced because it would blemish him, but an earlobe hole is not a blemish, so the piercing must be on the upper ear.

steps.title: What is the root of the tool dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the tool dispute and asks what each side's reasoning is. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים read the same פסוק but reach different rules. The גמרא wants to find the method of reading the פסוק that each one uses.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: 'They' are רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה from the tool dispute, not the earlobe dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the earlobe side question to the tool dispute
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the dispute between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about which tools may be used

steps.title: רבי reads the verse as a כלל ופרט וכלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads 'ולקחת' as a general term, 'מרצע' as a detail, and 'באזנו ובדלת' as another general term. So only things like the detail, metal tools, are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי expounds general terms and details. 'And you shall take' is a general term. 'An awl' is a detail. 'Through his ear and into the door' is a general term again. When there is a general term, a detail, and a general term, you include only things similar to the detail. Just as the detail is clearly metal, so too anything of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering its question by explaining רבי's method of reading the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי uses the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל: when a detail sits between two general terms, the general terms add only items that are like the detail. Since the awl is metal, any metal tool counts, but a thorn does not.

keyTerms.meaning: General terms and details; a method of reading פסוקים
General, detail, general; include only what is like the detail

steps.whatToRemember: רבי includes only metal tools because he reads the פסוק as a כלל ופרט וכלל, so only things like the awl count.

phrases.english: For Rabbi expounds general terms and details:
"And you shall take" is a general term.
"An awl" is a detail.
"Through his ear and into the door": it went back and generalized.
A general term, a detail, and a general term:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you may include only things similar to the detail.
Just as the clearly stated detail is made of metal,
so too anything made of metal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 13 by explaining רבי's side
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי reads the פסוק as כלל ופרט וכלל, so only tools similar to the awl, meaning metal tools, are included.

steps.title: רבי יוסי reads the verse as include, exclude, include
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses ריבוי ומיעוט. 'ולקחת' includes, 'מרצע' excludes, and 'באזנו ובדלת' includes again. The result is that almost everything is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי reads the verses as includings and excludings. 'And you shall take' includes. 'An awl' excludes. 'Through his ear and into the door' includes again. When the verse includes, excludes, and includes again, it has included everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering the question from step 13 by giving רבי יוסי's way of reading the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי read the same words as כלל ופרט וכלל, which only includes things similar to the detail, meaning metal tools. רבי יוסי reads them as ריבוי ומיעוט וריבוי, which includes almost everything and leaves out only one thing. So the two תנאים argue about which method of reading the verse to use.

keyTerms.meaning: a method of reading a verse as 'includings and excludings'
'and you shall take', the opening word of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two methods. כלל ופרט (רבי) includes only things like the detail. ריבוי ומיעוט (רבי יוסי) includes everything except one thing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one פסוק can give very different laws depending on which method of reading is used.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei expounds using includings and excludings:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who argued with רבי back in steps 9 and 10.

phrases.english: "And you shall take" includes.
"An awl" excludes.
"Through his ear and into the door" includes again.
phrases.notes: דברים 15:17

phrases.english: When it includes, excludes, and includes again,
it has included everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 14 by giving the second side of the disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי uses ריבוי ומיעוט וריבוי, which includes everything except one thing.

steps.title: What is included and what is left out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that everything is included, and only a chemical substance (סם) is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did it include? It included all things. What did it exclude? It excluded a chemical substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and answers in one breath: exactly what does רבי יוסי's reading include, and what single thing does it leave out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריבוי ומיעוט, the small 'exclusion' still has to leave something out. Here it removes a chemical that burns a hole, since that is the method least like an awl. Any tool that physically pierces is allowed.

phrases.english: What did it include?
phrases.notes: Here רבי means 'included'. It is not the name of the תנא רבי.

phrases.english: It included all things.
What did it exclude?
It excluded a chemical substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in practice what 'included everything' in step 15 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is included and excluded by רבי יוסי's reading?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every piercing tool is included. Only a chemical substance is excluded.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי: only metal tools. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: any tool, but not a chemical substance.

steps.title: How does 'the awl' show a large awl?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the teaching that 'המרצע' includes a large awl and asks where that is hinted in the word.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'The awl' comes to include the large awl. Where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the earlier teaching from step 10 and asks how the word shows it. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'המרצע' just means 'the awl'. Nothing obvious in it says 'big'. So the גמרא wants to know what in the word points to a large awl.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the Master said', used to quote an earlier teaching

phrases.english: The Master said:
"The awl" comes to include the large awl.
Where is this implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי and רבי יוסי argument and goes back to the second teaching in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the word 'המרצע' shows that a large awl is included?

steps.title: 'The' means the special one, like 'the thigh'
steps.stepSummary: Using רבא's teaching that 'הירך' means the most prominent part of the thigh, the גמרא explains that 'המרצע' means the special, outstanding awl.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: 'The thigh' means the most prominent part of the thigh. Here too, 'the awl' means the special one among awls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'the' (ה׳) points to the outstanding one of its kind, so here it points to the big awl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא learned that the extra 'ה' in 'הירך' points to the main, standout part. The same idea is applied to 'המרצע': the 'ה' points to the standout awl, which is the large one.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
"The thigh" means the most prominent part of the thigh.
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:33, the פסוק about the גיד הנשה.

phrases.english: Here too:
"The awl" means the special one among awls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'ה' points to the outstanding item of its kind, as with 'הירך', so it means the large awl.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the earlobe and the כהן slave, quoted again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the ברייתא: יודן בריבי says piercing is on the earlobe, and the חכמים say a כהן slave is not pierced because it would make him blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: יודן בריבי would teach: When they pierce, they pierce only on the earlobe. And the חכמים say: A Hebrew slave who is a כהן is not pierced, because he would become blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the ברייתא from steps 11 and 12 so it can ask a new question about it. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the ברייתא was used to show where on the ear the piercing is done. Now the גמרא focuses on a different point in it: the rule that a כהן slave is not pierced because of a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: a person with a blemish, which disqualifies a כהן from עבודה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Yudan the distinguished would expound:
When they pierce,
they pierce only on the earlobe.
And the Sages say:
A Hebrew slave who is a priest is not pierced
because he would become blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, יוּדָן בְּרִיבִּי הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of steps 11 and 12 to look at a new detail in it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is an עבד עברי is not pierced, because the piercing would make him a בעל מום.

steps.title: Why not let him become blemished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: so what if he becomes a בעל מום? Let him be pierced anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him become blemished!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים: why should the blemish stop the piercing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a בעל מום only stops a כהן from doing עבודה. It does not make him stop being a כהן. So why not pierce him, as the Torah commands for every slave who wants to stay?

phrases.english: So let him become blemished!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of the חכמים quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's rule that a כהן slave is not pierced because of the מום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Becoming blemished is not a forbidden act in itself, so it should not cancel the מצוה of רציעה.

steps.title: He must return to his full family status
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא answers from 'ושב אל משפחתו': the slave must be able to go back to his established status in his family, which for a כהן includes serving in the Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: The פסוק says, 'And he shall return to his family'. This means to his established status in his family.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק: the Torah wants the freed slave to go back to the same standing he had before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהן were pierced, he would leave slavery as a blemished כהן who can no longer do עבודה. That breaks the Torah's promise that he returns to his family's position. So the piercing is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and he shall return to his family'

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן עבד עברי is not pierced, because the Torah requires that he return to his full former status, including fitness for עבודה.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
The verse says: "And he shall return to his family"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:41

phrases.english: meaning to his established status in his family.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Becoming a בעל מום is no reason to skip the piercing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah requires that the freed slave return to his full family status, so a כהן may not be made unfit for עבודה.

steps.title: Can a master give a כהן slave a Canaanite maidservant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question: does the permission to give an עבד עברי a שפחה כנענית also apply when the slave is a כהן?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if a Hebrew slave is a כהן, may his master give him a Canaanite maidservant? Maybe it is a special exception that applies the same way to כהנים and ישראלים. Or maybe כהנים are different, since the Torah gave them extra מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks whether a master may give a כהן slave a שפחה כנענית, and it lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a Jew may not live with a non-Jewish woman, so the Torah's permission for an עבד עברי is a חידוש, a special exception. Side one says this exception covers everyone equally. Side two says כהנים have extra holiness rules, so the exception may not reach them.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)
A non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew
A special exception to the normal rules
Extra מצוות (here, the added rules that apply only to כהנים)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with the earlier piercing discussion. This question is not about the ear. It asks whether a כהן slave may be given a שפחה כנענית at all.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
A Hebrew slave who is a Kohen,

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר לוֹ רַבּוֹ שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית?
phrases.english: what is the law: may his master give him a Canaanite maidservant?
It is a special exception,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא כֹּהֲנִים וְלָא שְׁנָא יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: so there is no difference between Kohanim and regular Jews,
or perhaps Kohanim are different,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְרִיבָּה בָּהֶן הַכָּתוּב מִצְוֹת יְתֵירוֹת?
phrases.english: since the Torah gave them extra מצוות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new but related topic: a כהן who is an עבד עברי. This comes right after the discussion of why a כהן slave is not pierced.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the permission to give an עבד עברי a שפחה כנענית apply to a כהן too?

steps.title: רב permits, שמואל forbids
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a master may give a כהן slave a שפחה כנענית. שמואל rules that he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it is allowed. שמואל said: it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question just asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב follows the first side: the חידוש applies equally to everyone. שמואל follows the second side: the extra holiness of כהנים blocks the permission.

phrases.english: Rav said: It is allowed,
and Shmuel said: It is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: מוּתָּר, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers of the אמוראים to the question in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a master may give a כהן slave a שפחה כנענית. שמואל: he may not.

steps.title: רב נחמן scolds שמואל's students for missing a proof
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב ענן why the students of שמואל did not challenge him from the ברייתא that says a כהן slave is not pierced because he would get a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב ענן: when you learned in שמואל's house, were you playing games? Why didn't you challenge him from this ברייתא: the חכמים say a כהן who is a Hebrew slave is not pierced, because the piercing would give him a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן sharply questions why no one challenged שמואל. He points to the ברייתא from earlier as a source that goes against שמואל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives one specific reason a כהן is not pierced: piercing makes him a בעל מום. רב נחמן is hinting that this reason only makes sense if a כהן could otherwise qualify for piercing. The next step explains exactly why.

keyTerms.meaning: Game pieces or tokens, as if he were saying 'were you just playing around?'
Is pierced (has his ear pierced to stay a slave)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב עָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Anan:
When you were in the study hall of Mar Shmuel,
were you playing with game tokens?
phrases.notes: He means: weren't you taking your learning seriously?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תֵּימְרוּ לֵיהּ מֵהָא:
phrases.english: Why didn't you challenge him from this:
And the Sages say:
A Hebrew slave who is a Kohen is not pierced
because he would become blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תֵּימְרוּ לֵיהּ מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling from step 23 using the ברייתא from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a כהן slave may not be given a שפחה כנענית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's reason for not piercing a כהן (the מום) suggests that a כהן otherwise could be pierced. That would only be possible if he could have a שפחה.

steps.title: The proof explained: he could never say 'I love my wife and children'
steps.stepSummary: If a כהן could not receive a שפחה, the ברייתא would have used a simpler reason he cannot be pierced: he could never say 'I love my wife and my children.' So a כהן must be allowed a שפחה, and the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a master may not give him a שפחה כנענית, then I would already know he cannot be pierced. The slave must say 'I love my master, my wife and my children,' and a כהן would have no such wife and children. There is no answer to this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן spells out his proof against שמואל. The גמרא ends by saying there is no reply to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Piercing requires the slave to declare love for the wife and children his master gave him. If a כהן could never get a שפחה, that declaration would be impossible, and the מום reason would not be needed. Since the חכמים chose the מום reason, a כהן must be able to get a שפחה, which supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: I would already know it from (a simpler reason)
'I love my master', the declaration the slave must make before piercing
Nothing more can be said, meaning the proof stands unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא used the מום reason, not the 'no wife and children' reason. So a master may give a כהן slave a שפחה כנענית, like רב, and שמואל's view is refuted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא technique. When a source gives a harder reason, it implies the easier reason does not apply.

phrases.english: And if you say

phrases.aramaic: אֵין רַבּוֹ מוֹסֵר לוֹ שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית,
phrases.english: that his master may not give him a Canaanite maidservant,
I would already know he can't be pierced, since we need him to say:
"I love my master,
phrases.notes: שמות 21:5

phrases.english: my wife and my children,"
and he has none,
phrases.notes: Without a maidservant from his master, a כהן slave would have no such wife and children to say this about.

phrases.english: Nothing more can be said.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר אֵין רַבּוֹ מוֹסֵר לוֹ שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב נחמן's challenge in step 24 and closes the discussion.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a master may give a כהן slave a שפחה כנענית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's choice of the מום reason over the simpler 'no wife and children' reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof against שמואל stands unanswered. A כהן slave may be given a שפחה כנענית.

steps.title: Does the captive woman permission apply to a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a כהן soldier may take a יפת תאר, giving two sides to the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law for a כהן with a יפת תאר? Is it a special exception that applies the same to a כהן and a ישראל? Or are כהנים different, because the תורה gave them extra מצוות?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it asked about a כהן slave and a שפחה, the גמרא now asks whether a כהן may take a captive woman in war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says יפת תאר is a חידוש, a one-time special permission, so it covers everyone equally. The other side says כהנים carry extra holiness rules, so maybe the permission does not reach them.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
A beautiful woman captured in war, whom the תורה lets a soldier take
A special exception that breaks the normal rules
Extra מצוות (the added rules for כהנים)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
A כהן, what is the law with a beautiful captive woman?
phrases.notes: This is the war captive described in דברים 21:10-14.

phrases.english: Is it a special exception,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא כֹּהֵן וְלָא שְׁנָא יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: so it makes no difference whether he is a כהן or a ישראל,
or perhaps כהנים are different,
since the תורה added extra mitzvos for them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: כֹּהֵן, מַהוּ בִּיפַת תּוֹאַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question to the כהן slave and שפחה case, now about יפת תאר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the יפת תאר permission covers a כהן or whether his extra holiness rules exclude him

steps.title: רב permits, שמואל forbids
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a כהן may take a יפת תאר, and שמואל rules that he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it is permitted. שמואל said: it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question. The גמרא will now explain exactly what they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches their split in the slave case (step 23): רב is lenient for the כהן and שמואל is strict. The exact point of disagreement is not clear yet.

phrases.english: רב said: it is permitted,
and שמואל said: it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: מוּתָּר, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a כהן may take a יפת תאר. שמואל: he may not.

steps.title: Version one: everyone permits the first relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both agree the first relations are permitted, because the תורה allowed it only to deal with the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the first relations, everyone agrees it is permitted, because the תורה spoke only against the יצר הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument by first saying where רב and שמואל agree. This sets up the next step, which says where they do argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission exists because a soldier's desire in war is very strong, and a כהן has that same desire. So the first relations are permitted even for a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The first relations, during the war

keyTerms.term: לֹא דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד יֵצֶר הָרָע
keyTerms.meaning: The תורה spoke only to deal with the evil inclination

phrases.english: Regarding the first relations,
everyone agrees that it is permitted,
because the תורה did not speak
except to deal with the evil inclination.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּבִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute by stating where they agree
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In version one, the first relations are permitted for a כהן according to everyone.

steps.title: Version one: they argue about the second relations
steps.stepSummary: The real argument is about the second relations, when he brings her home and marries her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is the second relations. רב said: permitted. שמואל said: forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the exact point of the argument: the later stage, when the soldier takes her home and marries her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So now 'permitted' and 'forbidden' from step 27 refer only to marrying her afterward. The reasons come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The second relations, after he brings her home and marries her

phrases.english: Where they disagree is the second relations,
רב said: it is permitted,
and שמואל said: it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the narrowing by naming the point of dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In version one, רב and שמואל argue only about the second relations.

steps.title: The reasons of רב and שמואל in version one
steps.stepSummary: רב says once she was permitted she stays permitted. שמואל says she is now a גיורת, and a גיורת may not marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said it is permitted: since she became permitted, she stays permitted. שמואל said it is forbidden: because she is now a convert, and a convert is not fit for a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each side of the argument about the second relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב sees the whole יפת תאר process as one permission that carries through to the end. שמואל looks at her status at the time of marriage: by then she has converted, and a כהן may not marry a גיורת.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it was permitted, it stays permitted
A woman who converted to Judaism

phrases.english: רב said: it is permitted,
since she became permitted, she stays permitted.
And שמואל said: it is forbidden,
because she has become a convert,
and a convert is not fit for a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: מוּתָּר, הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתְּרַיא – אִישְׁתְּרַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of each side in version one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the permission carries through. שמואל: as a גיורת she is forbidden to a כהן.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא repeats 'רב אמר מותר ושמואל אמר אסור' on purpose. This time it is not a new argument; it is adding each side's reason.

steps.title: Version two: everyone forbids the second relations
steps.stepSummary: A second version says both agree the second relations are forbidden, because she is a גיורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: about the second relations, everyone agrees it is forbidden, because she has become a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of the argument. It starts by saying where both agree, which sets up the new point of dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here שמואל's reason from version one is accepted by everyone, even רב. So marrying her is out for a כהן, and the argument must move to the first relations.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (another version)

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: בְּבִיאָה שְׁנִיָּה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִירָא,
phrases.english: regarding the second relations, everyone agrees that she is forbidden,
because she has become a convert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בְּבִיאָה שְׁנִיָּה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the dispute, moving the agreement point
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In version two, the second relations are forbidden for a כהן according to everyone.

steps.title: Version two: רב permits the first relations
steps.stepSummary: In this version they argue about the first relations. רב permits it because the תורה allowed it to deal with the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is the first relations. רב said: permitted, because the תורה spoke only against the יצר הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the new point of argument and gives רב's reason. שמואל's side comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב uses the same reason that version one said everyone agreed to. The allowance answers the soldier's desire, which a כהן also has, even if he cannot marry her later.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is the first relations,
רב said: it is permitted,
because the תורה did not speak
except to deal with the evil inclination,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the dispute in version two and gives רב's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In version two, רב permits the first relations for a כהן.

steps.title: Version two: שמואל ties the first relations to marriage
steps.stepSummary: שמואל forbids the first relations: the פסוק allows taking her only when he can also bring her home as a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said it is forbidden. Wherever you can apply 'and you shall bring her into your house,' you can apply 'and you see among the captives.' Wherever you cannot apply 'and you shall bring her into your house,' you cannot apply 'and you see among the captives.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains why even the first relations are forbidden for a כהן. He links the beginning of the פסוקים to their end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's permission to take the captive comes as one package with marrying her at home. A כהן cannot marry her because she will be a גיורת, so the whole permission never starts for him.

keyTerms.meaning: We can apply (the פסוק) to it
And you shall bring her into your house
And you see among the captives

steps.whatToRemember: Version one: everyone permits the first relations, and they argue about marrying her (רב: the permission carries through; שמואל: a גיורת is forbidden to a כהן). Version two: everyone forbids marrying her, and they argue about the first relations (רב: it answers the יצר הרע; שמואל: no marriage means no permission at all).
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule in version two shows a key idea: the permission of יפת תאר is one unit. It only exists where the whole process, ending in marriage, can happen.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: the first relations are permitted only where marriage at home is possible, so a כהן is forbidden even at the start.

steps.title: The permission applies only during captivity, even to a married woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the יפת תואר rule applies only when he sees her during the war, and that it applies even if she is an אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "And you see among the captives" means at the time she is taken captive. "A woman" means even a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the פסוק of יפת תואר one word at a time. This step covers the first two lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בשביה' limits the permission to the time of captivity. He cannot use this rule for a woman he sees later, after the war. The word 'אשת' widens the rule: even a married non-Jewish captive is included.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught. This opens a ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the פסוק of יפת תואר word by word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יפת תואר permission applies only at the time of captivity, and it applies even to a married woman.

steps.title: The Torah allowed this only because of the evil inclination
steps.stepSummary: From 'יפת תואר' the ברייתא learns that the תורה gave this permission only to deal with the יצר הרע. It then begins a comparison: it is better for ישראל to eat meat...
steps.simpleTranslation: "A beautiful woman": the Torah spoke only in response to the evil inclination. It is better that Jews should eat the meat...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the תורה permitted the יפת תואר at all. It starts giving a comparison, and that comparison is finished in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יפת תואר' shows that he wants her because of her beauty, so this is a desire that comes from the יצר הרע. The תורה made an allowance for that desire instead of forbidding it outright. The words 'מוטב שיאכלו' open a 'better this than that' explanation, which the גמרא completes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman of beautiful appearance. This is the name for the captive woman the תורה permits.
The תורה spoke only... This means the rule was given for a specific reason.
In response to the evil inclination
It is better. This introduces a comparison between a lesser bad and a greater bad.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same phrase רב used in Step 32 to explain why he permits the first relations. So this ברייתא uses the very wording at the center of the מחלוקת.
